extracted.intended_audience: pipeline operators, pipeline safety compliance officers, industry stakeholders, and other parties subject to PHMSA pipeline safety regulations
extracted.subtask_description: Requirements and evaluation criteria for installation, operation, and equivalence demonstrations of rupture-mitigation valves (RMVs) and alternative technologies on onshore gas and hazardous liquid pipelines, including timing, notifications, flow modeling, and site-specific feasibility considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rupture identification as trigger for RMV operation
rubrics_metrics.description: PHMSA codified RMV operation response actions in §§192.636 and 195.419 to be keyed to rupture identification (not merely notification of potential rupture).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PHMSA declined to trigger RMV actions on notification of potential rupture to avoid procedural delays, but expects operators to have written procedures to identify a rupture upon notification. PHMSA may consider notification-based triggers in future rulemakings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Written procedures for identifying ruptures upon notification
rubrics_metrics.description: Operators must, upon notification of a potential rupture, identify whether there is indeed a rupture by reference to written procedures (codified at §§192.615(a)(12) and 195.402(e)(4)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Written procedures should incorporate common-sense elements, including waiver of requirements for specific pipeline personnel to conduct on‑scene investigation if one or more indicia are present (see rupture indicia criterion). Procedures should identify ruptures 'as soon as practicable.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Rupture indicia that can substitute for on-scene investigation
rubrics_metrics.description: Multiple or recurring instrument indications (pressure readings, alarms, etc.); pressure drops significantly in excess of minimum thresholds in §§192.635(a)(1) and 195.417(a)(1); and reports of rupture indicia from on‑scene, credible sources (e.g., pipeline personnel, sheriff/police, fire department, other emergency responders).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If one or more of these indicia are present, written procedures may waive requirements for specific personnel to perform on-scene investigation before identifying a rupture and actuating RMVs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Valve closure timeframe — 'as soon as practicable' with 30-minute ceiling
rubrics_metrics.description: Any RMVs and alternative equivalent technology installed pursuant to the final rule must be closed 'as soon as practicable' but no later than 30 minutes following the identification of a rupture.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 30-minute maximum replaced the NPRM's 40-minute ceiling. PHMSA emphasizes the 30-minute limit is a ceiling; operators are expected to close valves faster where practicable. ASVs and RCVs are expected to close faster than manual valves.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability by pipeline diameter and replacement status
rubrics_metrics.description: PHMSA requires that all valves on newly constructed or entirely replaced onshore gas transmission and gathering pipelines, and onshore hazardous liquid pipelines, with diameters ≥ 6 inches be RMVs or alternative equivalent technology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requirement applies to new construction and 'entirely replaced' pipelines (see definition criterion). New or entirely replaced laterals contributing 5 percent of the total volume of the applicable shut‑off segment also require RMVs. Implementation timeframe for construction/replacement requirements: 12 months following effective date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'entirely replaced' for triggering requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: PHMSA's rule uses a definition of 'entirely replaced' to determine when replacement triggers RMV installation requirements; Committees recommended applying the standard where multiple replacements, in aggregate, exceed 2 miles within a 5‑contiguous‑mile length within a 24‑month period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The definition is important to limit perverse incentives and to capture relevant replacement projects; PHMSA considered and revised the NPRM language in light of Committee recommendations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternative equivalent technology notification and demonstration
rubrics_metrics.description: Operators seeking to use an alternative equivalent technology in lieu of an RMV must submit an advance notification to PHMSA demonstrating the proposed technology provides an equivalent level of safety to an RMV.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the alternative is a manual valve, the operator must also demonstrate that installation of an RMV (ASV/RCV) would be economically, technically, or operationally infeasible. PHMSA developed an advance notification process at §§192.18 and 195.18 for site‑specific review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required content of site‑specific technical and safety evaluation for alternatives
rubrics_metrics.description: Notifications to PHMSA for alternative equivalent technology must include a site‑specific technical and safety evaluation with specified information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Required information includes design, construction, maintenance, and operating procedures; technology design and operating characteristics such as operation times (closure times for manual valves); service reliability and life; accessibility to operator personnel; nearby population density; potential consequences to the environment and the public; and any other information PHMSA requests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Factors demonstrating infeasibility of RMV installation
rubrics_metrics.description: Factors that may make installation of ASVs or RCVs infeasible include issues with communication signals, power sources, space for actuators, physical security, difficulty obtaining access rights or permits, prohibitive cost, component and labor availability, terrain, and accessibility to operator personnel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PHMSA acknowledged COVID‑19 exacerbated procurement and labor constraints. These factors can be cited in advance notifications or requests for extensions, but PHMSA expects planning for new construction/replacement to mitigate many constraints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Process to request exemptions or alternative shut‑off times
rubrics_metrics.description: Operators may request, under §192.18 (gas) or §195.18 (hazardous liquid), PHMSA review to: (1) install alternative equivalent technology; (2) request an exemption from the 30‑minute operation requirement for manual valves in certain locations; or (3) request that a valve remain open during emergency response if closing would be detrimental to public safety.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests must include information such as an estimated manual valve closure time and, for leaving a valve open, coordination with emergency responders, written procedures, and measures to minimize environmental impacts. PHMSA will review site‑specific cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations on exemptions by class/location
rubrics_metrics.description: PHMSA may allow operators to exceed the 30‑minute closure standard for manual valves only in limited settings (e.g., non‑HCA, Class 1 locations) if infeasibility is demonstrated; PHMSA did not include analogous exemptions for non‑HCA Class 2 locations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Class 2 locations pose greater public safety risk (10 to 45 houses near the pipeline) and therefore were not granted the same procedural machinery for exemptions in the final rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on leaving RMVs open during emergency response without prior approval
rubrics_metrics.description: PHMSA does not authorize operators, in conjunction with emergency responders, to leave RMVs or alternative equivalent technologies open for rupture mitigation or safety during emergency response without first forwarding a request to PHMSA under §§192.18 or 195.18 and developing appropriate written procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PHMSA believes isolation is paramount; any exceptions must be coordinated in advance with local emergency responders and approved by PHMSA, with specified written procedures for when to leave valves open and communication/mitigation plans.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flow modeling requirements for ASVs
rubrics_metrics.description: If an operator installs ASVs as RMVs, the operator must conduct flow modeling for the applicable pipeline segments and laterals to ensure the ASV will close within 30 minutes or less following rupture identification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Flow modeling must include anticipated maximum, normal, or other flow volumes, pressures, or operating conditions (including extreme weather effects) for up to a 15‑month period; model flow between RMVs and any looped pipelines or gas receipt tie‑ins; include a pressure drop/time chart or graph showing rupture segment isolation as soon as practicable and within 30 minutes. If operating conditions change, re‑model and reset ASV set pressures prior to the next review per §192.745.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rupture type and sizing considerations for flow model detection
rubrics_metrics.description: When conducting flow modeling for ASVs, operators should consider the type of rupture (e.g., pipe‑body or seam‑type) and size the pressure drop for rupture detection based on 0.5 times the pipe diameter (or less) pipe area when sizing the pressure drop for a rupture.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proper sizing affects detection sensitivity; incorrect modeling can lead to set pressures that render a 30‑minute closure time unachievable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shut‑off segment and RMV spacing
rubrics_metrics.description: Define 'shut‑off segment' as the segment of pipe between the RMVs closest to the upstream and downstream endpoints of an HCA, a Class 3 location, or a Class 4 location so that the entirety of these areas is between RMVs; multiple HCAs/Class 3/Class 4 locations can be contained in a single shut‑off segment; all valves installed on a shut‑off segment are RMVs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This definition is used to determine coverage and RMV placement; laterals contributing 5% of volume to a shut‑off segment also trigger RMV requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptable RMV types and allowance for check/locally actuated valves
rubrics_metrics.description: PHMSA used the term RMV to describe ASVs, RCVs, or alternative equivalent technology; commenters recommended including check valves, automated valves, EFRDs, locked/tagged manual valves, and locally actuated ASVs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Committee recommendations and PHMSA discussion noted check valves and locked/tagged crossover valves could be used as RMVs if they comply with spacing/operational requirements; PHMSA expects flexibility so long as the technology meets the closure/time standards and provides equivalent safety.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consistency with spill response plans and worst‑case discharge calculations
rubrics_metrics.description: Operators that have spill response plans indicating valve closure times of less than 30 minutes for worst‑case discharge scenarios must operate valves within the closure time indicated in their spill response plan (see §194.105(b)(1)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hazardous liquid pipeline operators must consider their shut‑down times when calculating worst‑case discharges and be able to close RMVs within that timeframe if it is less than 30 minutes.

rubrics_metrics.name: No differentiated closure times by valve type in the standard
rubrics_metrics.description: PHMSA did not assign different valve closure times to different rupture‑mitigating valves or technologies, because doing so would make compliance and enforcement difficult.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Instead, PHMSA sets a single ceiling (30 minutes) with the expectation operators will use appropriate technologies (ASV/RCV) where faster closure is achievable, and may seek alternative approvals when infeasible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advance procedural machinery for extensions of compliance timelines
rubrics_metrics.description: PHMSA established procedural machinery allowing operators to request extensions of compliance timelines for installation of RMVs and alternative equivalent technology where timelines are economically, technically, or operationally infeasible for near‑term construction and replacement projects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operators should use §§192.18 and 195.18 advance notification and extension request processes and provide supporting site‑specific information for PHMSA review.
